info.title: sumo-machine-manager SOVD — vendor extensions (x-*)
info.description: OpenAPI 3.1 description of the VENDOR EXTENSION surface (the `x-*` operations) exposed by the sumo-machine-manager SOVD servers. Every operation here is a vendor extension per the ISO 17978-1 extension rules — none is part of the ISO 17978-3 base surface, which this document deliberately does NOT annotate. For the ISO 17978-3 surface see the standard's own OpenAPI artifact (ISO 17978-3 ed.1 `openapi-specification-1.1.0-rc1.zip`, https://standards.iso.org/iso/17978/-3/ed-1/en/) and the sumo conformance file `docs/sovd_iso17978_spec.yaml` in the sumo-workspace (the 42/57 baseline). Auth: only `x-ota-pull-update` (POST) requires a bearer token (an Operational `update:execute` JWT bound to the device); the dev/sim `vm-sovd` binary defaults to open auth, so the requirement is advisory there.

post.summary: Build the node-level commit/rollback verdict routes.
post.description:
Wire (ISO 17978-3 §7.14 operation executions, at the **entity root**):

  `POST /vehicle/v1/operations/x-ota-commit-trials/executions`
  `POST /vehicle/v1/operations/x-ota-rollback-trials/executions`
  `POST /vehicle/v1/operations/x-update-verdict/executions` — the same two
       verdicts with `{"verdict": "commit"|"rollback"}` in a required body,
       on the same lock

The orchestrator issues ONE verdict per node per campaign step — the update
*session* is the commit unit, never a single component. Entity-root
addressing (no `{id}` segment) keeps these clear of the dynamic
`/components/{id}/operations/{op_id}/...` routes (mirrors the entity-root
`factory-reset` op) and means there is no per-component `/updates` session
to re-attach after the node reboot — membership is the NV-derived in-trial
set, identical before and after the reboot. Vendor extensions live here in
sumo-mm, not SOVDd (the three-layer rule, like `csr_router`).
`POST /vehicle/v1/operations/x-ota-commit-trials/executions` — the node
commit verdict; see [`node_verdict_router`] for the wire contract.

requestBody.description: Optional replay nonce; an absent or non-JSON body means no nonce (old-client shape).

200.description: Verdict applied across the node's in-trial components (`result.committed` / `skipped`).

409.description: Refused: a component's commit preflight reported Busy (awaiting reboot, selector/bank mismatch, provider pending reboot).

500.description: One or more components failed to commit (failed execution).

post.summary:
The POST handler: synchronous pre-flight (auth / anchor / L1 signature /
integrated-dep dispatch plan / busy check — every 4xx surfaces BEFORE the
202), then spawn the install task and reply `202 + Location`.

202.description: Accepted; the install runs in the background. Poll the `Location` for the execution.

Location.description: URL of the created execution resource.

400.description: L1 not base64, not a campaign, or an integrated dependency failed its dispatch plan.

401.description: Missing or insufficient Operational update:execute token bound to this device.

409.description: A pull-update execution is already running.

503.description: Device not provisioned: no sw-authority trust anchor.

parameters.name: execution_id
parameters.description: The execution id returned by the POST.

200.description: The execution's current status (running / completed / failed).

post.summary:
`POST /vehicle/v1/operations/x-ota-rollback-trials/executions` — the node
rollback verdict; see [`node_verdict_router`] for the wire contract.

requestBody.description: Optional replay nonce; an absent or non-JSON body means no nonce (old-client shape).

200.description: Verdict applied across the node's in-trial components (`result.rolled_back` / `skipped`).

409.description: Rollback was transiently refused by one or more components.

500.description: One or more components failed to roll back (failed execution).

post.summary:
`POST /vehicle/v1/operations/x-update-verdict/executions` — the node verdict
with the verdict in the body; exactly `x-ota-commit-trials` /
`x-ota-rollback-trials` under one operation id. See [`node_verdict_router`].

requestBody.description: Required JSON body: `verdict` (`commit` | `rollback`) plus an optional replay `nonce`. A missing or unknown `verdict` word is rejected with 422 (400 for malformed JSON, 415 without `Content-Type: application/json`).

200.description: Verdict applied across the node's in-trial components (`result.committed` or `result.rolled_back`, following the verdict, plus `skipped`).

409.description: Refused: every failure was a transient Busy refusal (e.g. a component's commit preflight).

500.description: One or more components failed to commit / roll back (failed execution).

BankContentsResponse.description: What one bank holds, by part name, as its installed manifest records it.

install_boot_id.description: The node boot id the bank was sealed in; `null` when unknown.

BankImageResponse.description: One installed image: its size in bytes and SHA-256 (lowercase hex).

ComponentBanksResponse.description:
One component's entry in the `banks` member: the active bank
and, for a two-bank component whose other bank holds an installed manifest,
the inactive one; `in_trial` = the component runs a not-yet-committed
install. An orchestrator compares `inactive` with its intent and downloads
only the images that differ.

pending_reset.description:
The newly installed content needs a node reset that has not happened
yet: the component needs a node reset to apply an install, and its
active bank was sealed in the node boot that is still running. `false`
when either boot id is unknown.

CsrRequest.description: Body of the `x-csr` operation: which key slot to generate a CSR for.

CsrResult.description:
The `result` of a successful `x-csr` execution: the requested slot and
its PKCS#10 CSR (DER, base64).

HsmKeyEntry.description:
One HSM key-slot entry in the [`HsmKeysResponse`] inventory — public
metadata only, never key material.

HsmKeysResponse.description:
The `hsm/data/keys` inventory: the device's provisioning state plus every
key slot.

NodeVerdictRequest.description:
Required POST body of the node `x-update-verdict` operation: the verdict,
plus the optional replay `nonce` echoed as in [`VerdictRequest`].

execution_id.description: Unique execution ID (for tracking async operations)

OperationStatus.description:
Status of an operation execution — ISO 17978-3 §7.14 line 387.

Spec-defined values: `running | completed | failed | stopped`.
(Pre-Phase-E variants `pending`/`cancelled` were non-spec and have
been removed — `pending` collapses to `running` once an execution
resource exists; `cancelled` is spelled `stopped` by the spec.)

cas_base_url.description:
Base URL of the content-addressed store the device pulls dependencies
and payloads from. Untrusted — every fetched blob is verified against
the signed content-address before use.

component.description:
Optional target assertion: when set, every dependency in the signed
campaign must target this component (400 otherwise). An ASSERTION, not
a filter — silently installing a subset of a signed campaign would
subvert the L1 as the decision artifact.

l1_base64.description:
The T2-signed L1 campaign manifest envelope (base64 of the COSE bytes).
Its dependency/payload URIs are content-addresses, so the device pins
what it fetches to what the signed manifest commits to.

ResolutionResponse.description:
How a node transaction ended: `outcome` is `committed` or `rolled_back`,
`reason` is `verdict` or `trial_boot_limit`.

UpdateStateResponse.description:
The `x-ota-update-state` resource body — the node's update-transaction
phase plus the component ids the transaction covers. `reboot_owed`:
components whose arming requires the node reboot and whose trial is
unresolved; `rebooted_since_arming`: whether the node boot id has changed
since that arming (null = unknown); `node_boot_id`: the node's current boot
id (null = unknown); `banks`: what each component's banks hold, per the
installed manifests (not a verification); `trial_boots`: node boots counted
while armed without a verdict (null = no boot-vector trial open or
resolved); `trial_boot_limit`: the count at which the node rolls itself
back (null = disabled); `resolution`: how the last node transaction ended,
per the boot vector (null = none recorded, or a trial is open).

VerdictExecution.description:
A verdict operation execution with the optional client `nonce` echoed back.
`#[serde(flatten)]` keeps the bare [`OperationExecution`] shape for old
clients (no nonce ⇒ the field is skipped); a supplied nonce is appended
verbatim as a top-level field.

VerdictRequest.description:
Optional POST body for the node-verdict operations. The client MAY supply a
`nonce` for replay-proofing — it is echoed verbatim in the execution record,
so a caller can tell its own fresh POST from a transport-level replay of an
earlier one. An absent body / non-JSON content type deserialises to `None`
(old clients, unchanged wire).

VerdictWord.description: The verdict word of the `x-update-verdict` body.
